components.name: Operational Action
components.description: An operational action in primary, secondary, pending, successful, failed, or denied states; brass marks intent, pigments report result.

narrative.overview: Hyperion renders one owner's deployed world as a compact latitude atlas: horizontal Applications, Services, and Foundations territories hold service routes, an inline dossier appears only for the selected route, a narrow bearings rail summarizes state, and logs remain closed until requested. Warm mineral fields and carbon type do the daily work; rare brass marks identity, focus, selection, and direct routes. The operations-console extension adds Overview, Schedules, Units, and Activity workspaces as descendants of the same world: host metric instruments live in one ruled field, operational actions report consequences in operational pigment, and the Atlas itself remains the preserved incumbent surface.
keyCharacteristics: Horizontal latitude bands, coordinate margins, and shared cartographic rules instead of a card grid.
Dense .56rem–.85rem supporting type with a compact Recursive statement scale.
Rare brass for orientation and action; independent pigments for service state.
Dossiers and logs provide operational depth on demand.
A global shell of five workspaces that extends the atlas world without replacing it.
Truthful telemetry instruments and consequential operational actions inside the same ruled system.

rules.name: The Rare Metal Rule
rules.body: Brass never indicates health and should occupy less than ten percent of a screen. Its rarity makes orientation and selection immediate.

rules.name: The Dense Instrument Rule
rules.body: Supporting type intentionally lives between .56rem and .85rem; essential actions and service names occupy the upper end while tertiary telemetry occupies the lower end.

rules.name: The Instrument-Only Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace styling belongs to endpoints, timestamps, coordinates, shortcut keys, and logs—never general navigation or decorative labels.

rules.name: The Cartographic Layer Rule
rules.body: Use tone and seams to explain hierarchy at rest. Shadow means an element has actually lifted above the atlas.

rules.name: The Workspace Rule
rules.body: Navigation is a seam, not a screen change. The shell is the same continuous ruled field; only the active latitude changes.

rules.name: The Truthful Instrument Rule
rules.body: Hyperion never manufactures a percentage, rate, temperature, or history it did not observe. Missing evidence is written as absent.

rules.name: The Consequence Rule
rules.body: Operational actions look consequential through exact labels, expected-state checks, and confirmed impact—never through color, glow, or motion. Brass marks intent; operational pigments report the result.

dos: Do preserve the find, read state, open service sequence; reveal dossiers and logs only on demand.
Do keep direct service access visually ahead of logs, health traces, and diagnostics.
Do use shared horizontal bands, plotted rules, coordinates, and alignment to make the deployed world feel mapped.
Do preserve the .56rem–.85rem supporting scale and 4/5/8/13px radius ladder as intentional density choices.
Do retain text labels, visible brass focus, and reduced-motion behavior alongside visual cues.
donts: Don't turn the latitude bands into an interchangeable rounded-card grid or a monitoring wall.
Don't use Greek letters, blue Mediterranean palettes, columns, laurels, amphorae, or temple silhouettes.
Don't make gold a background treatment, a health state, or a decorative glow.
Don't enlarge every supporting label into ordinary body copy and erase the atlas's instrument hierarchy.
Don't add decorative shadow to static surfaces or let logs compete with the primary route-opening workflow.
